== Biography ==
James Glasgow was baptised on 19 March 1626 at Inveresk and Musselburgh, Midlothian, Scotland, as a son of [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]].<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-GQW record VQ4V-GQW], James Glasgow, 19 March 1626, Inveresk and Musselburgh, son of Alexander Glasgow (accessed 2025).</ref> [[Clerk-296|Jannet Clerk]] is retained as his uncertain mother from the reconstructed Inveresk household; the reviewed index names only Alexander.

== Research Notes ==
=== Fisherrow and Murieston family ===
Alexander [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]]’s existing fatherhood of James [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]] is individually assessed at 98%, strongly supported, within the record-defined Inveresk family. The freshly re-read Findmypast R_686178012 gives James, birth year 1626, Inveresk with Musselburgh, father Alexander Glasgow and no mother or baptism date. The maintained FamilySearch VQ4V-GQW citation supplies19 March 1626. These derivatives are not independent witnesses to the baptism. The saved WikiTree father was already confident; this is a numeric assessment, not a new father or outstanding certainty upgrade. The proposed 1716 writer identity is assessed separately and does not change this child’s parentage. Findmypast SCOT/OPR/BUR/0189706 reports James Glasgow, writer, died11 October 1716 and buried14 October 1716, aged87; OPR685_1/86, item2, p.318, Edinburgh. Its 1629 birth year is calculated from age, not a recorded birth. Prefer this as a possible later identity of the Inveresk child James-3923 at 45%: the uncommon name, Midlothian setting and a three-year difference from the 1626 baptism make a useful comparison. No occupation is otherwise established for that child. This remains below probable: there is no parent, spouse, residence or career bridge, and another unrepresented James is a substantial possibility. [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] is the separately recorded Edinburgh weaver, son of Robert of Wester Duddingston; [[Glasgow-3332|James Glasgow]] is the unresolved Biggar/Quothquan/Lindsaylands weaver comparison. Their different occupations and age estimates weaken these matches without excluding them. Findmypast’s suggested records are automated leads, not corroboration. The 1716 death and writer occupation remain a candidate association; no structured birth or death field is changed.<ref>Scottish Record Office,Index to Edinburgh etc.sasines 1624–1630,pp.187–188,8 July 1624,RS25 9/135, [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015072481057&seq=193 printed index]; James Maidment,Analecta ScoticaI(1834),art.CXVI,pp.395–396,399,[https://archive.org/details/analectascotica00maidgoog volume]; NRS Mid Calder OPR694/10,p.7,17 February 1605,previously inspected original; Findmypast,[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_686178012&tab=this R_686178012],Inveresk 1626,father Alexander; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F0189706&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BUR/0189706],Edinburgh 1716,OPR685_1/86,item2,p.318. Indexes/transcripts; the 1716 adult identity is possible only.</ref>


This child is distinct from [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]], the Edinburgh weaver and burgess. The latter's 1641 apprenticeship explicitly names his father as Robert Glasgow of Wester Duddingston.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666'', p. 71, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up 16 June 1641].</ref> The two profiles should not be merged.

The structured birth about 1626 and Inveresk/Musselburgh location are derived from the baptism and remain uncertain as birth details.
